top news.title: Nvidia announces the RTX Spark, an Arm-based consumer chip family it calls “the most efficient PC chip ever built”, made on TSMC 3 in partnership with MediaTek

tweets.author: @satyanadella
tweets.text: Our goal is to deliver unmetered intelligence to every home and every desk with Windows. NVIDIA RTX Spark marks a real breakthrough toward that vision. Looking forward to sharing more with Jensen, who will be joining us live from Taiwan, at Build this week!

tweets.author: @zacbowden
tweets.text: NVIDIA says its RTX Spark Windows on Arm chips will run every Windows app ever made, squashing concerns that some x86 apps or games won't be compatible. It seems the company is confident that buyers won't need to be worried about some apps not being compatible.

tweets.author: @mweinbach
tweets.text: I was talking to someone about it yesterday Apple silicon was so well architected from the start to just offer the best perf per watt and unified memory, chiplets, Arm, large cache, etc Then as AI made you push your hardware more, the benefits of these choices started to show

sub_items.title: Microsoft unveils the Surface Laptop Ultra, featuring an Nvidia RTX Spark SoC, a 15" mini-LED touchscreen, and up to 128GB of unified memory, coming this fall
Jensen Huang says Microsoft and Nvidia will “reinvent the PC”, starting with 30+ laptops and 10 desktops coming in the fall from Dell, HP, ASUS, Lenovo, and MSI
Nvidia says RTX Spark offers up to 20 CPU cores and a Blackwell GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores, capable of “100 FPS 1440p gaming” or running 120B-parameter AI models

top news.title: Anthropic says it has confidentially filed for an IPO, which could happen as soon as this fall, joining OpenAI and SpaceX in preparing to go public in 2026

tweets.author: @danprimack
tweets.text: Anthropic filing confidentially now seems to put it on a path to go public well before Labor Day... Or at least gives it the optionality. Big companies rarely price into summer vacations, but this already is an outlier for so many reasons.

tweets.author: @dee_bosa
tweets.text: worth noting: filing first ≠ pricing first a confidential draft S-1 starts the SEC clock but sets no date

tweets.author: @quinnypig
tweets.text: “Confidentially submitted a draft registration statement.” Translation: Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia would like their money back now please, and the private rounds have officially run out of road.

top news.title: Hackers say they used Meta's AI support chatbot to change emails tied to Instagram accounts, amid a wave of high-profile account takeovers; Meta fixed the issue

tweets.author: @wongmjane
tweets.text: Even my Instagram account got hacked The password got changed without my knowledge and I was getting different password reset attempts throughout yesterday. And I got repeatedly logged out from the IG iOS app Quite concerning

tweets.author: @heaney555
tweets.text: This is arguably the biggest security fuckup in the history of mainstream social media. Meta should be ashamed for letting this happen, and it should be triggering a serious rethink across the tech industry of how AI is used for customer support.

tweets.author: @gergelyorosz
tweets.text: What I'm hearing: Instagram's Trust and Safery org absolutely gutted the last few weeks. ~60% of the org gone - between layoffs and forced reassignments to data labelling. All while “AI maxxing” pushed a bunch of bugs to prod. And hence why today's massive Insta account takeover
